\section[il volante]{il volante — a steering wheel}

\label{lesson:IT-C254-volante}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for a form, then the Italian for a vehicle seat.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: il volante}
\textbf{il volante} — \textquotedblleft{}a steering wheel\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{volante} is the present participle of \emph{volare}, \textquotedblleft{}to fly\textquotedblright{}, used as a noun, after French \emph{volant}: the wheel that spins. \emph{volare} $\leftarrow$ Latin \emph{volare}. (EtymDB 2.1)
\end{cousinweb}
